title: Vertical differentiation signal maps (unofficial)
content:
Purpose: quick, sales-friendly synthesis of where Redwood wins and where to be careful for five priority verticals. This is an agile note (unofficial) to help SDRs, AEs, and product marketing ask better discovery questions and choose proof points. Treat as living: feedback loop -> PRD/Playbook (confluence)

Status & context:
- Pulled from customer interviews (Q4 2024–Q1 2025), two recent pilots (healthcare payer, fintech payments), and SRE telemetry on latency/regional failover.
- Goal: produce signal maps (concise decision heuristics) that map buyer risk -> Redwood capabilities -> immediate sales assets.
- Not a final playbook; next steps: map to one-pagers, create battlecards, and run an enablement workshop week of 2025-03-24.

How to read this doc (quick):
- For each vertical we list: top buyer priorities, primary objections, Redwood advantage(s), attacker moves (competitors’ plays), and 2–3 sales-ready scripts / demo hooks.
- Use the scripts as templates not verbatim lines; localize for customer size and procurement maturity.

1) Fintech (payments & consumer fintech)
- Buyer priorities: PCI scope minimization, low tail latency for high-velocity flows, predictable per-transaction cost, deterministic throughput at peak batch windows (settlement runs), data residency (for regional regulators).
- Primary objections: "We already host models internally", "cost is too variable", "we can't have model drift that affects compliance-affecting outputs".
- Redwood advantages: Dedicated capacity + explicit throughput SLOs (predictable cost), private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for PCI scope reduction, intelligent routing to keep low-latency regional nodes, caching for repeated pattern inference (KYC templates).
- Competitor plays to watch: Large cloud AI vendors push integrated billing + tokenization to stay in-cloud; self-host venders pitch full control and cost-caps.
- Sales demo hooks / scripts:
  - Hook: "We can pin throughput and guarantee XX qps for settlement windows — reduces your p99 during peak by ~40% in our pilots."
  - Security emphasis: "When you deploy Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS, counsel can narrow PCI scope; we’ll provide a compliance checklist (pilot playbook)."
  - Objection handling: "If you run models internally, consider a hybrid: keep sensitive model pieces on-prem, use Redwood routing for burst capacity and dedicated endpoints for predictable cost."

2) Healthcare (payers, digital therapeutics)
- Buyer priorities: HIPAA, audit trail + explainability, longitudinal data residency, FDA/clinical validation process for decisioning, deterministic outputs for patient-facing content.
- Primary objections: "Black box outputs are unacceptable", "we need audit/kind-of-LLM explainability for regulators".
- Redwood advantages: Private control plane (audit logs), per-token attribution and traceability in Console, rollout controls (canary/A-B rollback) support slow clinical validation. Integration patterns for EHR proxies and de-identified prefix caching.
- Competitor plays: Niche vendors hype specialized medically-tuned models; incumbent cloud providers bundle their EMR partners.
- Sales demo hooks / scripts:
  - Hook: "We attach full request/response audit trails and model versioning to each inference — auditors and clinical reviewers can replay decisions."
  - Clinical validation angle: "Run canary cohorts with Redwood rollouts and automatic fallback to a certified model if outputs deviate beyond your defined drift thresholds."

3) Legal & Regulated Knowledge Workflows
- Buyer priorities: data retention controls, e-discovery defensibility, accuracy in citations, minimization of hallucination, on-prem or air-gapped options for privileged data.
- Primary objections: "LLMs make stuff up; we can't risk bad legal advice".
- Redwood advantages: deterministic serving (version pinning, quantization profiles to reduce variability), reranking/verification pipelines, integrated evaluation hooks (safety checks pre-send), private deployments and HSM support.
- Competitor plays: specialized legal LLM vendors tout tight retrieval-augmented systems; general LLM providers push large context windows.
- Sales demo hooks / scripts:
  - Hook: "We pair a verification reranker and policy checks in the serving path so your counsel can see source links, confidence signals, and model provenance per reply."
  - Proof point: "Pilot with top-20 firm reduced ‘citation failure’ events by X% (internal pilot data) — we can run a short POC on a sandbox corpus."

4) Enterprise SaaS (product-embedded AI features)
- Buyer priorities: embed-first dev ergonomics, predictable unit economics, runtime controls (latency budgets), multi-tenant isolation, simple SDKs.
- Primary objections: "Too many moving parts to integrate; we don't want to manage ops".
- Redwood advantages: Hosted API for fast time-to-value + Dedicated for scale, SDKs that mirror the same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, Optimize recommendations to reduce cost per inference without changing UX.
- Competitor plays: API-first LLM providers emphasize a huge model catalog; infrastructure vendors offer turnkey inference but with higher ops lift.
- Sales demo hooks / scripts:
  - Hook: "Ship a feature using Redwood Hosted in a day; when usage grows, swap to Dedicated without code changes — same API, same SDKs."
  - Cost pitch: "We provide unit-cost optimization playbooks and a console that shows token-level spend per route — you can spot hot prompts and throttle them."

5) Government & Defense (contracting, classified workloads)
- Buyer priorities: FedRAMP / IL compliance, data sovereignty, long-tail availability under constrained procurement, on-prem or air-gapped install capabilities, strict supply chain attestations.
- Primary objections: "Procurement and C2 classification will kill timelines", "no vendor-managed secrets".
- Redwood advantages: Private deployments with customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs and binary attestations, an on-prem package and partner engineering to help with STIGs and authority to operate (ATO) artifacts.
- Competitor plays: Big cloud providers offer GovCloud and bundled ATOs; defense-specific vendors tout hardened appliances and cleared staff.
- Sales demo hooks / scripts:
  - Hook: "We provide a hardened on-prem reference and a gap analysis against your STIG/ATO checklist; partner engineers can scope an ATO pathway."
  - Procurement tactic: "Start with a table-top non-prod integration to validate interface and security posture while procurement runs in parallel."

Cross-vertical themes & enablement asks:
- Common buyer language: predictability (cost & latency), traceability (audit logs & model versions), and a pragmatic path to isolation (Dedicated -> Private). Package messaging around these three pillars.
- Compelling assets we need now:
  1) One-pager "Predictable inference economics for regulated apps" (target: fintech+healthcare+gov).
  2) Short demo scripts for each vertical + 5-min video walkthrough of Console trace + model rollout.
  3) An ATO checklist template and PCI scoping checklist to hand to security teams.
- Tactical objections & quick counters (one-liners):
  - "We need full control of models" -> "Hybrid: keep training/inference-sensitive paths private, and use Redwood for burst/throughput with routing policies."
  - "Risk of hallucination" -> "We chain a lightweight verifier and show provenance in the response; canary rollouts catch regressions early."
  - "Cost unpredictable" -> "Dedicated reservations, predictable SLOs, and Optimize recommendations cut unit cost — we'll build a cost forecast for your peak patterns."

Open questions / research tasks (next 30 days):
- Collate and anonymize pilot metrics (p99 latency, cost per 1M tokens, incident reports) for sales playbooks. (Owner: Priya)
- Create a public-facing compliance checklist (Ava) and a gated ATO pack we can hand to procurement (Diego).
- Build two short console demo videos: 1) trace/replay + audits, 2) rollout/canary reversal (Riley).

Notes to enablement lead: prioritize fintech and healthcare one-pagers first — the pipeline there is most mature and deals are sensitive to the messages in this doc. We'll iterate to full playbooks after the March enablement week.

Slack/refs: see thread #gtm-verticals for recent pilot quotes; shortlist in confluence: GTMP/verticals/summary-2025 (linked above).

End of note.
